Lemma
[Continuity of logarithmic entropy] Source: chow-et-al-ricci-flow-part-iii:page-0047 1. ch17:17.25\group Entropy Minimizers

For every $\delta >0$, the map \[ w\longmapsto \int _{\mathcal M}w^2\log w^2\, d\mu \] is continuous in $L^{2(1+\delta )}$, and hence in $W^{1,2}$ on a closed manifold.
Proof

\sketch The mean value theorem writes the pointwise difference as $(|w_2|-|w_1|)2a(1+\log a^2)$ with $a$ between $|w_1|$ and $|w_2|$. Cauchy–Schwarz applies because $|a\log a|\le \max \{ e^{-1},(\delta e)^{-1}a^{1+\delta }\} $. Thus the difference of the integrals tends to zero with the $L^{2(1+\delta )}$ distance. Sobolev embedding supplies the last assertion.

□
